A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework. Their text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across renaming, renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original MATH-500 and AMC evaluations, a pass@64 follow-up, ablations and worked examples in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those results and adds token-cost measurements, an existence-only control, another NL-model comparison and a physics evaluation.

M1.justification: The alignment, mixed problem input, FL reasoning, answer extraction and random FL-output dropping procedures are retained. NFL-HR is a rename, and Appendix F explains an existing component. The additional model experiment applies the existing framework.

E1.justification: Appendix C.3 extends evaluation from mathematical QA to physics using PhysReason-mini: the first sub-question from each of 200 problems, with images replaced by captions. This adds a substantive domain and input scenario while retaining MATH-500 and AMC.

E2.justification: New Tables 6–7 add an NL existence-problem solver control and a pure-NL DeepSeek-R1-Distilled-8B-0528 baseline in the corresponding experiments. The original Qwen3 comparison and ablation comparators remain.

E3.justification: The original pass@16/pass@64 procedures, temperatures and 8192-token limit remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce generated-token measurements, a second NL-model configuration, and first-sub-question selection with caption substitution for the physics evaluation.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands the analytical questions tested: Appendix C.1 examines whether existence reformulation alone explains gains, C.2 tests dependence on the NL model, and Section 3.5 measures computational overhead. The original ablations and mismatched-input case study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The retained pass@16/pass@64 sampling budgets are evaluation procedures, not new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original headline, subject-level, pass@64 and ablation scores remain unchanged. New Table 6 reports existence-only NL scores of 53.01%/70.20% on AMC/MATH-500. Table 7 reports DeepSeek NL scores of 77.11%/86.20% versus NFL-HR's 81.93%/89.40%. Physics results are 22.50% versus 26.50%, and Table 3 adds average token counts of 5458.42 versus 6310.35. These are substantial additional results under their stated settings.

T1.justification: The existential reformulation, prover notation and mathematical content of the appendix examples are retained. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or substantive derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same framework contributions, headline accuracies and claims about solving problems difficult for NL reasoning. Broader integration of expert knowledge was already claimed in v1's Discussion; the physics experiment supplies additional support.

C2.justification: Appendices E–F clarify verification's role in pretrained FL capability and explain fallback through ill-posed existence formulations, degree/radian mismatches and invalid Lean statements. Appendix C and Section 3.5 add interpretations of format effects, generalization and cost tradeoffs. The original limitation concerning direct formal validation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly documents the pretrained models' training sources, the 7B autoformalizer and QwQ-32B-assisted expert iteration. The introduction changes planned code release to stated availability at the same repository link, although the conclusion retains future tense. Original prompts and inference settings remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to PhysReason, ProofNet and Compfiles, plus a brief discussion of MATP-Bench and multimodal formal reasoning. The broader positioning relative to NL reasoning, formal provers and formal answer selection remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 adopts the NFL-HR abbreviation, makes localized prose and contact-text edits, and inserts a computation-cost subsection and Appendices C–F. Earlier Appendices C–E become G–I. Most existing narrative, prompts and worked-example text are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds tables for token cost, the existence-only control and the DeepSeek comparison. Existing tables are relocated or renumbered, and appendix listings lose line numbers and receive revised syntax highlighting. The existing figures and overall document layout remain recognizable.

improvement.justification: Appendix C adds a useful control for the reformulation explanation and checks another model and domain, strengthening support for the retained contribution. Token measurements and concrete formalization limitations improve transparency. These are valuable supplementary gains; the claim of similar GPU costs remains qualitative, and direct formal validation remains unresolved.
